q: The Brown–Fisher–Hurtado theorem (2020) resolves Zimmer's conjecture for SL(n,ℤ) by proving:
opts: All lattice actions on manifolds are trivial
For n≥3, any C∞ volume-preserving action of SL(n,ℤ) on a compact manifold of dimension <n-1 factors through a finite group action
exp: BFH (Annals 2022): SL(n,ℤ) cannot act faithfully on manifolds of dimension <n-1 by smooth volume-preserving diffeomorphisms. The proof uses KAM theory, cocycle superrigidity, and non-stationary normal forms — a mix of analysis and representation theory.
